history.period: Medieval (protected monument; founding date not documented)
history.summary: The Kalyanji (Kalyan Rai Ji) temple of Todaraisingh is one of the town's 50+ historic temples and is listed as a protected monument by the National Monuments Authority ('Kalyanraiji's Temple', standing on a high platform in plain terrain within Todaraisingh; coordinates taken from the NMA listing). FLAG - distinct from the famous Diggi Kalyanji (Malpura tehsil, Tonk district, rebuilt 1527 CE under Rana Sanga), which most web sources and listings describe; the Todaraisingh temple has no separately published founding history - do not import Diggi's legend (King Digva/Urvashi) here. The town itself is ancient: founded by the Nagas c. 4th century (Takshakagadha/Todapattan), ruled by Yuhilas and Ajmer Chauhans, capital of the Solanki Rajputs in the 15th-16th centuries, and named for Rai Singh Sisodia, a Mughal mansabdar under Shahjahan. Other notable sites include Hadi Rani ki Baori and the temples of Raghoraiji, Gopinathji and Govinddeoji.

name: Kalyanji Temple, Todaraisingh
town_description: Toda Rai Singh (Todaraisingh) is an ancient, hill-surrounded town in Tonk district, Rajasthan, about 48 km from Tonk and 135 km from Jaipur. Noted for its archaeological significance, stepwells (Hadi Rani ki Baori, Isar Baori, Bhopat Baori) and over 50 historic temples, it is locally famous for 'ghatti, patti, bawdi, dawdi'.

travel.railway: Tonk has no railway station; nearest major railheads Jaipur (~135 km) and Sawai Madhopur (~85 km, verify)
travel.road: ~48 km from Tonk town by road; buses and taxis from Tonk and Jaipur
